children: While insurance regulator Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a major reform in distribution norms by sharply cutting commission payouts across products to bring down distribution costs and benefit customers, the steep cut could make insurance distribution unviable, forcing distributors to completely rethink their business models.

The proposed changes could also have implications for banks. As bancassurance commissions constitute an important source of fee income for many banks, particularly private sector banks, any reduction in commission payouts could therefore affect earnings from this business.

IRDAI, which released its much-awaited public consultation paper on insurance distribution reforms aimed at lowering policy costs and curbing mis-selling, said the purpose of these reforms is to facilitate better and more sustainable outcomes for all stakeholders, specifically policyholders.

The consultation paper proposed expense of management (EoM) for life insurance companies to be 15 per cent of their gross direct premium income (GDPI) in two years and 12.5 per cent in five years, and 20 per cent of GDPI in five years in the case of non-life insurance companies, including standalone health insurance companies (SAHI), from the existing 30 per cent. Moreover, the EoM calculation is being changed to exclude reinsurance inward and consider only a third of crop insurance in gross premiums.

According to industry participants and analysts, the proposals made would reintroduce commission caps across life, health and motor insurance that IRDAI had scrapped in 2023. It has proposed drastic cuts in first-year commissions across life savings and term, health and motor.

Commissions on health renewals and porting have been proposed to be cut drastically to 5 per cent in case of distribution entities and 10 per cent in the case of agents. Commission caps based on distribution lines have been proposed with lower limits for banks/brokers versus agents. While renewal commissions have been linked to persistency in life insurance, higher commissions have been allowed for premiums from smaller tier cities, similar to mutual funds.

Under the proposed rules, banks and non-bank lenders would be barred from compulsorily bundling insurance with loans. Also, single premium credit life commissions are capped at 2 per cent. Significantly, at present, the average effective payouts on single-premium group credit life is around 45 per cent.

“IRDAI’s distribution consultation paper proposes stricter EoM limits for insurers, and 1/2-1/3rd commission cuts in health, term and motor insurance. This is a risk for PB Fintech/Turtlemint, noting 10 per cent cut in new business commission rates translate to 10-12 per cent fall in their earnings,” Jefferies said in its report on Thursday.

The brokerages, in its report, said SBI Life Insurance and LIC with EoM ratios of 10.6 per cent and 11.9 per cent respectively, are comfortably placed. Others would need to reduce commissions to meet the new EoM threshold. “This could be a risk to near-term growth, with insurers with strong agency better placed. Lower commissions could also result in banks (HDFC Bank, Axis) with open architecture pushing their key life insurance partners,” Jefferies said.

According to it, in the non-life insurance segment, Star Health and Allied Insurance should be at lower risk due to its agency dominance. GoDigit General Insurance and ICICI Lombard General Insurance would face risk of slower motor own damage growth, as commissions have been cut by a third. However, in the medium term, lower commissions may reduce competition in motor insurance, benefitting these general insurance companies.

Emkay Research, in its report, said the intent behind the proposed reform could be noble, to address the root cause behind mis-selling and also to make insurance more affordable. “However, the drastic cut in distribution commission would also make insurance distribution an unviable business and an unattractive vocation. And this could severely backfire, hurting the regulator’s growth agenda and ‘Insurance for All’ by 2047,” Emkay pointed out in its report. It said SBI LIFE Insurance, LIC, and Star Health and Allied Insurance will be among the less-impacted, while HDFC LIFE Insurance, Axis Max Life Insurance and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance will have to get their distribution economics right to comply with the proposed commission and EOM structure.

“Bancassurance commissions constitute an important source of fee income for many banks, particularly private sector banks. Any reduction in commission payouts could therefore affect earnings from this business, though the impact is not expected to be material for most banks,” said Neha Parikh, Vice-President, Sector Head — Financial Sector Ratings, ICRA.

According to IIFL Capital, banking system bancassurance pool of  $2.2 billion grew at 28 per cent CAGR in the last three years, constituting 10 per cent of banks’ fee income. “With relatively lower contribution from credit-life payouts, we think actual PAT impact is likely to be only low single-digit for banks,” it said in a report.
According to a top official at a large insurance distributor, the IRDAI reforms proposals reverse the 2023 EoM changes and may increase compliance costs without benefiting policyholders.

However, Bejon Kumar Misra International Consumer Policy Expert & EC Member, General Insurance Council, said the proposed distribution reforms are an important step towards making insurance more affordable, transparent and accountable to the policyholder. “For too long, high upfront commissions have created incentives to sell what is most rewarding to the distributor rather than what is most suitable for the consumer. Staggering commissions over the life of a policy can better align the interests of the insurer, intermediary and policyholder and discourage mis-selling and unnecessary policy churn,” Misra pointed out.

“These reforms can directly benefit customers through lower costs, greater choice and reduced mis-selling. Better-aligned commissions can encourage need-based advice, helping customers make more informed decisions and get better value from their insurance over the long term,” said Saibal Biswas, founder and mentor, Saibal Biswas and Associates.

title: IRDAI’s major reform agenda to force distributors to completely rethink business models, can impact earnings of banks
